fields.name: I
fields.text: Master interrupt enable: when 0, no interrupt is enabled whatever the individual enables say; when 1, the per-source enables in their own registers decide. Hardware clears it when an interrupt is taken and RETI sets it again; SEI sets it and CLI clears it.

fields.name: T
fields.text: One-bit store for bit copies: BST copies a bit of a Register File register into T, and BLD copies T into a bit of a register.

fields.name: H
fields.text: Set when some arithmetic operations produce a half carry; used in BCD arithmetic.

fields.name: S
fields.text: Sign bit, always N exclusive-OR V.

fields.name: V
fields.text: Two's complement overflow flag, for signed arithmetic.

fields.name: N
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic operation gives a negative result.

fields.name: Z
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic operation gives a zero result.

fields.name: C
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic operation gives a carry.

registers.name: EEARH
registers.title: EEPROM Address Register
notes: Initial value of bit 0 printed as X/0.

fields.name: EEAR8
fields.text: EEPROM address bit 8, the top address bit on ATtiny85; reserved and read as 0 on ATtiny25/45. EEAR resets to an undefined value, so write an address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEAR7
fields.text: EEPROM address bit 7, the top address bit on ATtiny45; reserved and read as 0 on ATtiny25. EEAR resets to an undefined value, so write an address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEAR
fields.text: Low EEPROM address bits; bytes are addressed linearly from 0 to 127, 255 or 511 depending on device. EEAR resets to an undefined value, so write an address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: On a write, the byte to store at the EEAR address; on a read, the byte fetched from the EEAR address.

fields.name: EEPM
fields.text: Selects what a write of EEPE does: erase and write together as one atomic operation, erase only, or write only. Writes to EEPM are ignored while EEPE is set. Reset returns it to 0b00 unless the EEPROM is busy programming.

rows: Erase and write as one atomic operation

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: EEPROM Ready interrupt enable: 1 enables it when the SREG I-bit is set, 0 disables it. The interrupt fires continuously while non-volatile memory is ready to program.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: EEPROM master program enable: while set, setting EEPE within 4 clock cycles programs the EEPROM at the chosen address; while 0, setting EEPE does nothing. Hardware clears it 4 clock cycles after software sets it.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: EEPROM program strobe: writing 1 programs the EEPROM as EEPM selects, but only if EEMPE was written to 1 first. Hardware clears it when the write time has passed. Setting it halts the CPU for 2 cycles before the next instruction.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: EEPROM read strobe: with the address in EEAR, writing 1 reads the EEPROM; the data is ready at once, in one instruction, and the CPU halts for 4 cycles. A read cannot be done and EEAR cannot be changed while a write is in progress; poll EEPE before reading.

registers.name: OSCCAL
registers.title: Oscillator Calibration Register
notes: Initial value of bits 7:0 printed as Device Specific Calibration Value.

fields.name: CAL
fields.text: Trims the internal RC oscillator frequency. Reset loads the factory calibration value; software may write another. CAL7 picks the low (0) or high (1) frequency range, the ranges overlapping so 0x7F runs faster than 0x80; CAL[6:0] tunes within the range from 0x00 (lowest) to 0x7F (highest). The oscillator times EEPROM and Flash writes: above 8.8 MHz those writes may fail. Change the value in steps of at most 0x20, since a cycle-to-cycle frequency change over 2% can make operation unpredictable, and hold the MCU in reset during such changes. Calibration outside the specified range is not guaranteed.

registers.name: CLKPR
registers.title: Clock Prescale Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: CLKPCE
fields.text: Prescaler change enable: must be written to 1, with all other CLKPR bits written 0 at the same time, before CLKPS can change. Hardware clears it 4 cycles after the write or when CLKPS is written; writing it again within those 4 cycles neither extends nor clears it.

fields.name: CLKPS
fields.text: Divides the selected clock source down to the system clock, slowing all synchronous peripherals; may be changed at run time. To change it, write CLKPCE=1 with the other bits 0, then within 4 cycles write the new CLKPS with CLKPCE=0, with interrupts disabled. Reset value is 0000 when the CKDIV8 fuse is unprogrammed and 0011 (divide by 8) when it is programmed; parts ship with CKDIV8 programmed. Any value can be written whatever the fuse. In ATtiny15 compatibility mode the prescaler is off and the system clock is 1.6 MHz.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: BOD sleep: turns the brown-out detector off during sleep, on devices that have this. Set by a timed sequence: write BODS and BODSE both to 1, then within 4 clock cycles write BODS=1 and BODSE=0. BODS takes effect 3 clock cycles after being set and clears itself after 3 more; a SLEEP executed while it is active turns the BOD off for that sleep. Reads 0 on devices without sleeping BOD.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up Disable.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Sleep enable: must be 1 for the SLEEP instruction to put the MCU to sleep. Setting it just before SLEEP and clearing it right after waking keeps the MCU from sleeping by accident.

fields.name: SM
fields.text: Selects which of the three sleep modes SLEEP enters.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: BOD sleep enable: allows BODS to be set as part of the timed BOD-disable sequence. Reads 0 on devices without software BOD disable.

fields.name: ISC01
fields.text: Interrupt Sense Control 0, bit 1.

fields.name: ISC00
fields.text: Interrupt Sense Control 0, bit 0.

fields.name: PRTIM1
fields.text: Writing 1 shuts down Timer/Counter1; when it is enabled again it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRTIM0
fields.text: Writing 1 shuts down Timer/Counter0; when it is enabled again it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRUSI
fields.text: Writing 1 stops the USI clock, shutting the USI down; reinitialise the USI after waking it.

fields.name: PRADC
fields.text: Writing 1 shuts down the ADC, which must be disabled first. Parts of the analog comparator use the ADC clock, so the comparator cannot be used while this bit is 1.

registers.name: MCUSR
registers.title: MCU Status Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Set by a watchdog reset; a power-on reset clears it, as does writing 0.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Set by a brown-out reset; a power-on reset clears it, as does writing 0.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: Set by an external reset; a power-on reset clears it, as does writing 0.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Set by a power-on reset; cleared only by writing 0. Reading and then clearing MCUSR early in the program lets the flags show the source of the next reset.

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Set on a watchdog time-out when the watchdog is set for interrupt. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. With the SREG I-bit and WDIE set, the time-out interrupt runs.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: Watchdog interrupt enable: with WDE clear and the SREG I-bit set, a time-out runs the interrupt instead of resetting. With WDE set, hardware clears WDIE on a time-out, so the next time-out resets unless WDIE is set again after each interrupt.

fields.name: WDP3
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 3, the top bit of WDP[3:0], which sets the time-out period while the watchdog is enabled. Reserved settings from 0b1010 up select one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Watchdog change enable: must be set to write WDE to 0 or to change the prescaler bits; hardware clears it 4 clock cycles after it is written to 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: Watchdog enable: 1 enables the watchdog timer, 0 disables it, but WDE can only be cleared while WDCE is 1. To disable: write 1 to both WDCE and WDE in one operation (WDE written 1 even if already 1), then within 4 clock cycles write WDE=0. In safety level 2 the watchdog cannot be disabled. In safety level 1, WDRF in MCUSR overrides WDE, keeping it set while WDRF is set, so clear WDRF before disabling. If the watchdog is unused, run the disable procedure, clearing WDRF and WDE, at initialisation, since an accidental enable would reset the device repeatedly.

fields.name: WDP2
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 2 of WDP[3:0], which sets the time-out period while the watchdog is enabled. Reserved settings from 0b1010 up select one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDP1
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 1 of WDP[3:0], which sets the time-out period while the watchdog is enabled. Reserved settings from 0b1010 up select one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDP0
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 0 of WDP[3:0], which sets the time-out period while the watchdog is enabled. Reserved settings from 0b1010 up select one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: BOD Sleep.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up Disable.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Sleep Enable.

fields.name: SM1
fields.text: Sleep Mode select bit 1.

fields.name: SM0
fields.text: Sleep Mode select bit 0.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: BOD Sleep Enable.

fields.name: ISC0
fields.text: Selects the level or edge on the INT0 pin that triggers External Interrupt 0, which runs when the SREG I-flag and its mask are set. The pin is sampled before edges are detected: for edge or toggle sensing, a pulse longer than one clock period triggers it and shorter ones may not; for low level, the level must last until the current instruction completes.

fields.name: INT0
fields.text: External interrupt 0 enable: with this bit and the SREG I-bit set, the INT0 pin interrupt is enabled, sensed as MCUCR ISC01/ISC00 select, and runs from the INT0 vector. Pin activity triggers it even when INT0 is an output.

fields.name: PCIE
fields.text: Pin change interrupt enable: with this bit and the SREG I-bit set, a change on any PCINT[5:0] pin enabled in PCMSK triggers an interrupt from the PCI vector.

fields.name: INTF0
fields.text: Set when an edge or logic change on INT0 raises an interrupt request; with the SREG I-bit and GIMSK INT0 set, the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs or by writing 1. Stays 0 while INT0 is set for level sensing.

fields.name: PCIF
fields.text: Set when any PCINT[5:0] pin changes level and raises an interrupt request; with the SREG I-bit and GIMSK PCIE set, the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCINT
fields.text: One bit per I/O pin: 1 enables the pin change interrupt on that pin when GIMSK PCIE is also set; 0 disables it.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: BOD Sleep.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the pull-ups on all I/O ports, even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn are set to enable them ({DDxn, PORTxn} = 0b01).

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Sleep Enable.

fields.name: SM1
fields.text: Sleep Mode select bit 1.

fields.name: SM0
fields.text: Sleep Mode select bit 0.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: BOD Sleep Enable.

fields.name: ISC01
fields.text: Interrupt Sense Control 0, bit 1.

fields.name: ISC00
fields.text: Interrupt Sense Control 0, bit 0.

fields.name: PORTB5
fields.text: Port B data bit 5, for pin PB5.

fields.name: PORTB4
fields.text: Port B data bit 4, for pin PB4.

fields.text: Port B data bit 3, for pin PB3.

fields.name: PORTB0

notes: Initial value of bits 5:0 printed as N/A.

fields.text: Port B input pin bit 5, for pin PB5.

fields.name: PINB0

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: Timer/counter synchronization mode: while 1, the value written to PSR0 is held, keeping the prescaler in reset so the timer/counter stays halted while it is configured. Writing 0 makes hardware clear PSR0, and counting starts.

fields.name: PWM1B
fields.text: Pulse Width Modulator B Enable (Timer/Counter1).

fields.name: COM1B1
fields.text: Comparator B Output Mode bit 1 (Timer/Counter1).

fields.name: COM1B0
fields.text: Comparator B Output Mode bit 0 (Timer/Counter1).

fields.name: FOC1B
fields.text: Force Output Compare Match 1B.

fields.name: FOC1A
fields.text: Force Output Compare Match 1A.

fields.name: PSR1
fields.text: Prescaler Reset Timer/Counter1.

fields.name: PSR0
fields.text: When 1, resets the Timer/Counter0 prescaler. Hardware clears it at once unless TSM is set.

fields.name: COM0A
fields.text: Sets how the OC0A pin behaves on compare match; any nonzero setting makes OC0A override the pin's normal port function, though its DDR bit must still be set to enable the output driver. The meaning depends on the WGM0[2:0] mode. In fast PWM, when OCR0A equals TOP and COM0A1 is set, the compare match is ignored and the set or clear happens at BOTTOM; in phase correct PWM, likewise at TOP.

fields.name: WGM0
fields.text: Low two waveform generation mode bits; with WGM02 in TCCR0B they set the counting sequence, where TOP comes from, and the waveform type: normal, CTC, or one of two PWM modes. MAX is 0xFF and BOTTOM is 0x00.

registers.name: TCCR0B
registers.title: Timer/Counter Control Register B
notes: The settings of WGM02 are carried on TCCR0A.WGM0, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: FOC0A
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, changing OC0A as COM0A[1:0] set; it is a strobe, so the COM0A value at that moment decides the effect. Active only in non-PWM modes; write it 0 whenever TCCR0B is written in a PWM mode. It raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR0A as TOP. Always reads 0.

fields.name: FOC0B
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, changing OC0B as COM0B[1:0] set; it is a strobe, so the COM0B value at that moment decides the effect. Active only in non-PWM modes; write it 0 whenever TCCR0B is written in a PWM mode. It raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR0B as TOP. Always reads 0.

fields.name: WGM02
fields.text: Waveform generation mode bit 2; works with WGM0[1:0] in TCCR0A.

fields.name: CS0
fields.text: Selects the Timer/Counter0 clock source. With an external T0 clock, edges on T0 clock the counter even when the pin is an output, so software can drive the count.

values.text: External clock on T0, falling edge.
External clock on T0, rising edge.

fields.name: TCNT0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 count value.

fields.name: OCR0A
fields.text: Output Compare Register A value for Timer/Counter0.

fields.name: OCR0B
fields.text: Output Compare Register B value for Timer/Counter0.

fields.name: OCIE1A
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Match A Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCIE1B
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Match B Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCIE0A
fields.text: With this bit and the SREG I-bit set, the Timer/Counter0 compare A interrupt is on; it runs when a compare match sets OCF0A in TIFR.

fields.name: OCIE0B
fields.text: With this bit and the SREG I-bit set, the Timer/Counter0 compare match B interrupt is enabled; it runs when OCF0B in TIFR is set by a compare match.

fields.name: TOIE1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Overflow Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: TOIE0
fields.text: With this bit and the SREG I-bit set, the Timer/Counter0 overflow interrupt is enabled; it runs when TOV0 in TIFR is set by an overflow.

fields.name: OCF1A
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 1A.

fields.name: OCF1B
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 1B.

fields.name: OCF0A
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter0 and OCR0A. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. With the SREG I-bit, OCIE0A and OCF0A set, the compare match A interrupt runs.

fields.name: OCF0B
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter0 and OCR0B. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. With the SREG I-bit, OCIE0B and OCF0B set, the compare match B interrupt runs.

fields.name: TOV1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Overflow Flag.

fields.name: TOV0
fields.text: Set when Timer/Counter0 overflows; when it is set depends on the WGM0[2:0] setting. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. With the SREG I-bit, TOIE0 and TOV0 set, the overflow interrupt runs.

fields.name: CTC1
fields.text: When 1, Timer/Counter1 goes back to 0x00 one CPU clock cycle after it matches OCR1C; when 0, it keeps counting through compare matches.

fields.name: PWM1A
fields.text: When 1, enables PWM mode on comparator OCR1A, and the counter goes back to 0x00 one CPU clock cycle after it matches OCR1C.

fields.name: COM1A
fields.text: Sets the action on pin PB1 (OC1A) after a compare match with compare register A; the pin's direction bit must be 1 for it to drive the pin. OC1A is not connected in normal mode. These bits work differently in PWM mode.

fields.name: CS1
fields.text: Selects the Timer/Counter1 prescaler source; the stop setting acts as a timer enable/disable.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: Timer/Counter Synchronization Mode.

fields.name: PWM1B
fields.text: When 1, enables PWM mode on comparator OCR1B, and the counter goes back to 0x00 one CPU clock cycle after it matches OCR1C.

fields.name: COM1B
fields.text: Sets the action on pin PB4 (OC1B) after a compare match with compare register B; the pin's direction bit must be 1 for it to drive the pin. OC1B is not connected in normal mode. These bits work differently in PWM mode.

fields.name: FOC1B
fields.text: Writing 1 changes pin PB4 (OC1B) as COM1B1 and COM1B0 set, as if a compare match had happened but with no interrupt, whatever the timer value; if COM1B is written in the same cycle, the new setting applies. Not used while PWM1B is set. Always reads 0.

fields.name: FOC1A
fields.text: Writing 1 changes pin PB1 (OC1A) as COM1A1 and COM1A0 set, as if a compare match had happened but with no interrupt, whatever the timer value; if COM1A is written in the same cycle, the new setting applies. Not used while PWM1A is set. Always reads 0.

fields.name: PSR1
fields.text: Writing 1 resets the Timer/Counter1 prescaler, leaving TCNT1 as it is; hardware clears the bit once done. Writing 0 does nothing. Always reads 0.

fields.name: PSR0
fields.text: Prescaler Reset Timer/Counter0.

fields.name: TCNT1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 count value.

fields.name: OCR1A
fields.text: Output Compare Register A value for Timer/Counter1.

fields.name: OCR1B
fields.text: Output Compare Register B value for Timer/Counter1.

fields.name: OCR1C
fields.text: Output Compare Register C value for Timer/Counter1.

fields.name: OCIE1A
fields.text: With this bit and the SREG I-bit both 1, Timer/Counter1 raises its compare A interrupt, from vector $003, on a compare match A, which sets the compare flag in TIFR.

fields.name: OCIE1B
fields.text: With this bit and the SREG I-bit set, the Timer/Counter1 compare match B interrupt is enabled; it runs from vector $009 on a compare match B, which sets the compare flag in TIFR.

fields.name: OCIE0A
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Output Compare Match A Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCIE0B
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Output Compare Match B Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: TOIE1
fields.text: With this bit and the SREG I-bit set, the Timer/Counter1 overflow interrupt is enabled; it runs from vector $004 on a Timer/Counter1 overflow, which sets the overflow flag in TIFR.

fields.name: TOIE0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Overflow Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCF1A
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter1 and OCR1A. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1, which takes effect after a synchronization clock cycle. With the SREG I-bit, OCIE1A and OCF1A set, the compare match A interrupt runs.

fields.name: OCF1B
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter1 and OCR1B. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1, which takes effect after a synchronization clock cycle. With the SREG I-bit, OCIE1B and OCF1B set, the compare match B interrupt runs.

fields.name: OCF0A
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 0A.

fields.name: OCF0B
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 0B.

fields.name: TOV1
fields.text: In normal mode (PWM1A and PWM1B both 0), set when Timer/Counter1 overflows; in PWM mode (PWM1A or PWM1B 1), set on a compare match between Timer/Counter1 and OCR1C. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1, which takes effect after a synchronization clock cycle. With the SREG I-bit, TOIE1 and TOV1 set, the overflow interrupt runs.

fields.name: TOV0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Overflow Flag.

registers.name: PLLCSR
registers.title: PLL Control and Status Register
notes: Initial value of bit 1 printed as 0/1.

fields.name: LSM
fields.text: Low speed mode: writing 1 halves the fast peripheral clock from 64 MHz to 32 MHz. Required below 2.7 V supply, where Timer/Counter1 cannot run fast enough. Stop Timer/Counter1 when changing it. Cannot be set while PLLCLK is the system clock.

fields.name: PCKE
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 clock source: 1 selects asynchronous mode, clocked by PCK at 64 MHz (32 MHz in low speed mode); 0 selects synchronous mode, clocked by the system clock CK. Can be set only once PLLE is set, and is safe to set only when PLOCK is 1.

fields.name: PLLE
fields.text: Setting it starts the PLL, and the internal RC oscillator as its reference if needed. Always 1 when the PLL is the system clock source.

fields.name: PLOCK
fields.text: Reads 1 when the PLL is locked to its reference clock. Ignore it during the first lock-in, while the PLL frequency overshoots and undershoots; steady state comes within 100 us. Checking it after lock-in, before enabling PCK for Timer/Counter1, is recommended.

fields.name: CTC1
fields.text: When 1, Timer/Counter1 goes back to 0x00 one CPU clock cycle after it matches OCR1A; when 0, it keeps counting through compare matches.

fields.name: PWM1A
fields.text: When 1, enables PWM mode on comparator OCR1A, and the counter goes back to 0x00 one CPU clock cycle after it matches OCR1C.

fields.name: COM1A
fields.text: Sets the action on pin PB1 (OC1A) after a compare match with compare register A; the pin's direction bit must be 1 for it to drive the pin. These bits work differently in PWM mode.

fields.name: CS1
fields.text: Selects the Timer/Counter1 prescaler source; the stop setting acts as a timer enable/disable.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: Timer/Counter Synchronization Mode.

fields.name: PWM1B
fields.text: Pulse Width Modulator B Enable.

fields.name: COM1B1
fields.text: Comparator B Output Mode bit 1.

fields.name: COM1B0
fields.text: Comparator B Output Mode bit 0.

fields.name: FOC1B
fields.text: Force Output Compare Match 1B.

fields.name: FOC1A
fields.text: Writing 1 changes pin PB1 (OC1A) as COM1A1 and COM1A0 set, as if a compare match had happened but with no interrupt, whatever the timer value; if COM1A is written in the same cycle, the new setting applies. Not used while PWM1A is set. Always reads 0.

fields.name: PSR1
fields.text: Writing 1 resets the Timer/Counter1 prescaler, leaving TCNT1 as it is; hardware clears the bit once done. Writing 0 does nothing. Always reads 0.

fields.name: PSR0
fields.text: Prescaler Reset Timer/Counter0.

fields.name: TCNT1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 count value; it counts up and can be read and written. A write reaches the counter one CPU clock cycle late in synchronous mode, and at most two in asynchronous mode.

fields.name: OCR1A
fields.text: Value compared continuously with Timer/Counter1; a match happens only when the counter counts to it, not when software writes TCNT1 and OCR1A to the same value. A match sets OCF1A after a synchronization delay.

fields.name: OCR1C
fields.text: Value compared continuously with Timer/Counter1, in place of the ATtiny15's OCR1B and doing the same job; a match happens only when the counter counts to it, not when software writes TCNT1 and OCR1C to the same value. With CTC1 set, a match clears TCNT1.

fields.name: OCIE1A
fields.text: With this bit and the SREG I-bit both 1, Timer/Counter1 raises its compare A interrupt, from vector $003, on a compare match A, which sets the compare flag in TIFR.

fields.name: OCIE1B
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 Output Compare Match B Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCIE0A
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Output Compare Match A Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCIE0B
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Output Compare Match B Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: TOIE1
fields.text: With this bit and the SREG I-bit set, the Timer/Counter1 overflow interrupt is enabled; it runs from vector $004 on a Timer/Counter1 overflow, which sets the overflow flag in TIFR.

fields.name: TOIE0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Overflow Interrupt Enable.

fields.name: OCF1A
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter1 and OCR1A. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1, which takes effect after a synchronization clock cycle. With the SREG I-bit, OCIE1A and OCF1A set, the compare match A interrupt runs.

fields.name: OCF1B
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 1B.

fields.name: OCF0A
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 0A.

fields.name: OCF0B
fields.text: Output Compare Flag 0B.

fields.name: TOV1
fields.text: Set when Timer/Counter1 overflows. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1, which takes effect after a synchronization clock cycle. With the SREG I-bit, TOIE1 and TOV1 set, the overflow interrupt runs.

fields.name: TOV0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 Overflow Flag.

registers.name: PLLCSR
registers.title: PLL Control and Status Register
notes: Initial value of bit 1 printed as 0/1.

fields.name: LSM
fields.text: Low Speed Mode.

fields.name: PCKE
fields.text: PCK enable; always 1 in ATtiny15 compatibility mode.

fields.name: PLLE
fields.text: PLL enable; the PLL is always on in ATtiny15 compatibility mode.

fields.name: PLOCK
fields.text: Reads 1 when the PLL is locked to its reference clock. Ignore it during the first lock-in, while the PLL frequency overshoots and undershoots; steady state comes within 100 us. Checking it after lock-in, before enabling PCK for Timer/Counter1, is recommended.

fields.name: DTPS1
fields.text: Division factor of the dead time prescaler ahead of the dead time generator: it divides the Timer/Counter1 clock (PCK or CK) by a factor of 1, 2, 4 or 8.

fields.name: DT1AH
fields.text: High four bits of the OC1A dead time, counted in prescaled timer/counter clocks; from zero up to 15 prescaled clock periods.

fields.name: DT1AL
fields.text: Low four bits of the OC1A dead time, counted in prescaled timer/counter clocks; from zero up to 15 prescaled clock periods.

fields.name: DT1BH
fields.text: High four bits of the OC1B dead time, counted in prescaled timer/counter clocks; from zero up to 15 prescaled clock periods.

fields.name: DT1BL
fields.text: Low four bits of the OC1B dead time, counted in prescaled timer/counter clocks; from zero up to 15 prescaled clock periods.

fields.name: USIDR
fields.text: USI data register.

fields.name: USIBR
fields.text: USI buffer register.

fields.name: USISIF
fields.text: Start condition flag: in two-wire mode, set when a start condition is detected; in three-wire or output-disabled mode, set by any edge on SCK. With USISIE and the global interrupt enable set, it raises an interrupt. Cleared only by writing 1, which in two-wire mode also lets go of USCL held by start detection. The interrupt wakes the CPU from all sleep modes.

fields.name: USIOIF
fields.text: Set when the 4-bit counter overflows from 15 to 0. With USIOIE and the global interrupt enable set, it raises an interrupt. Cleared only by writing 1, which in two-wire mode also lets go of SCL held by a counter overflow. The interrupt wakes the CPU from Idle.

fields.name: USIPF
fields.text: In two-wire mode, set when a stop condition is detected; cleared by writing 1. Not an interrupt flag; useful for two-wire bus master arbitration.

fields.name: USIDC
fields.text: Data output collision: 1 when bit 7 of USIDR differs from the pin's actual level. Valid only in two-wire mode; useful for two-wire bus master arbitration.

fields.name: USICNT
fields.text: Current value of the 4-bit counter, readable and writable by the CPU. It counts up once per clock from the external clock edge detector, a Timer/Counter0 compare match, or the USICLK or USITC strobes, as USICS[1:0] select. With an external clock source (USICS1=1) and USICLK written 1, writing USITC clocks it. The external clock input (USCK/SCL) can clock the counter even with USIWM[1:0]=0.

fields.name: USISIE
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the start condition interrupt; with a pending interrupt and the global interrupt enable set, it runs at once.

fields.name: USIOIE
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the counter overflow interrupt; with a pending interrupt and the global interrupt enable set, it runs at once.

fields.name: USIWM
fields.text: Selects the wire mode. It changes only how the outputs behave: data and clock inputs work the same in every mode, so the counter and USIDR can be clocked externally and data sampled even with outputs disabled. In two-wire mode DI and USCK are called SDA and SCL.

values.text: Outputs, clock hold and start detector disabled; pins work as normal port pins.

Three-wire mode on DO, DI and USCK. DO overrides its PORTB bit, but DDRB still sets its direction and, as an input, PORTB sets its pull-up. DI and USCK leave normal port operation alone. As master, clock pulses come from software toggling PORTB with the pin as output, for which USITC can be used.

Two-wire mode on SDA (DI) and SCL (USCK), both bidirectional with open-collector outputs enabled by their DDRB bits. An enabled SDA is pulled low when the USIDR output or its PORTB bit is 0, otherwise released. An enabled SCL is pulled low when its PORTB bit is 0 or by the start detector, otherwise released; it is held low after a detected start condition until USISIF is cleared. Inputs are unaffected; pull-ups on SDA and SCL are disabled.
Two-wire mode on SDA and SCL as 0b10, except SCL is also held low after a counter overflow until USIOIF is cleared.

fields.name: USICS
fields.text: Selects the clock for USIDR and the counter. With an external clock (USCK/SCL), the output latch changes the output on the edge opposite the one that samples DI/SDA; with the software strobe or Timer/Counter0 compare match, the latch is transparent and the output changes at once. USICS[1:0]=00 selects the software strobe, where writing USICLK=1 clocks both USIDR and the counter. With USICS1=1, USICLK instead chooses between external clocking and USITC strobe clocking of the counter.

fields.name: USICLK
fields.text: With USICS[1:0]=00, writing 1 shifts USIDR one step and increments the counter; the output changes in the same instruction cycle, and the bit shifted in was sampled in the previous cycle. With an external clock (USICS1=1), setting it makes the USITC strobe the counter's clock instead. Reads 0.

fields.name: USITC
fields.text: Writing 1 toggles USCK/SCL, whatever the DDR setting, though the DDR bit must be 1 for the pin to show it; useful for generating a master clock. With an external clock (USICS1=1) and USICLK=1, writing it clocks the 4-bit counter directly, so a master can tell early when a transfer ends. Reads 0.

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: BIN
fields.text: Bipolar Input Mode.

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: When 1 and the ADC is off (ADCSRA ADEN=0), the ADC multiplexer picks the analog comparator's negative input; when 0, AIN1 is the negative input.

fields.name: IPR
fields.text: Input Polarity Reversal.

fields.name: ADTS2
fields.text: ADC Auto Trigger Source bit 2.

fields.name: ADTS1
fields.text: ADC Auto Trigger Source bit 1.

fields.name: ADTS0
fields.text: ADC Auto Trigger Source bit 0.

registers.name: ACSR
registers.title: Analog Comparator Control and Status Register
notes: Initial value of bit 5 printed as N/A.

fields.name: ACD
fields.text: Writing 1 switches off power to the analog comparator, reducing consumption in Active and Idle; may be set at any time. Clear ACIE before changing it, or the change can raise an interrupt.

fields.name: ACBG
fields.text: When 1, a fixed bandgap reference replaces AIN0 as the comparator's positive input; when 0, AIN0 is used. The bandgap takes time to settle, and the first conversion before it settles may be wrong.

fields.name: ACO
fields.text: Comparator output, synchronized, which delays it by 1 to 2 clock cycles.

fields.name: ACI
fields.text: Hardware sets it when the comparator output does what ACIS1/ACIS0 select. With ACIE and the SREG I-bit set, the comparator interrupt runs. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: ACIE
fields.text: With this bit written 1 and the SREG I-bit set, the analog comparator interrupt is enabled; written 0, it is disabled.

fields.name: ACIS
fields.text: Selects which comparator event raises the comparator interrupt. Clear ACIE before changing these bits, or the change can raise an interrupt.

fields.name: ADC0D
fields.text: ADC0 Digital Input Disable.

fields.name: ADC2D
fields.text: ADC2 Digital Input Disable.

fields.name: ADC3D
fields.text: ADC3 Digital Input Disable.

fields.name: ADC1D
fields.text: ADC1 Digital Input Disable.

fields.name: AIN1D
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the digital input buffer on the AIN1 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Set it when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused, to save power in the buffer.

fields.name: AIN0D
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the digital input buffer on the AIN0 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Set it when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused, to save power in the buffer.

fields.name: REFS1
fields.text: Voltage reference selection bit 1; with REFS2 and REFS0 it chooses the ADC reference. A change during a conversion takes effect when that conversion completes (ADIF set), and the next conversion after any change takes 25 ADC clock cycles. With differential channels and gain, a VCC reference or an external AREF above VCC - 1 V is not recommended, as it affects accuracy. The 2.56 V reference needs a supply of 3 V.

rows: VCC as reference, disconnected from PB0 (AREF).
External reference on PB0 (AREF); internal reference off.
Internal 2.56 V reference, no external bypass capacitor, disconnected from PB0 (AREF).
Internal 2.56 V reference with an external bypass capacitor on PB0 (AREF).

fields.name: REFS0
fields.text: Voltage reference selection bit 0; with REFS2 and REFS1 it chooses the ADC reference. A change during a conversion takes effect when that conversion completes (ADIF set), and the next conversion after any change takes 25 ADC clock cycles. With differential channels and gain, a VCC reference or an external AREF above VCC - 1 V is not recommended, as it affects accuracy. The 2.56 V reference needs a supply of 3 V.

fields.name: ADLAR
fields.text: Writing 1 left-adjusts the conversion result in the ADC data register; otherwise it is right-adjusted. A change applies to the data register at once, even during a conversion.

fields.name: REFS2
fields.text: Voltage reference selection bit 2; with REFS1 and REFS0 it chooses the ADC reference. A change during a conversion takes effect when that conversion completes (ADIF set), and the next conversion after any change takes 25 ADC clock cycles. With differential channels and gain, a VCC reference or an external AREF above VCC - 1 V is not recommended, as it affects accuracy. The 2.56 V reference needs a supply of 3 V.

fields.name: MUX
fields.text: Selects which analog inputs feed the ADC and, for the differential pairs ADC0-ADC1 and ADC2-ADC3, the gain. ADC0 or ADC2 on both inputs gives an offset measurement, for offset calibration only. Single-ended ADC4 selects the temperature sensor. A change during a conversion takes effect when that conversion completes (ADIF set). After switching to the internal reference the ADC needs 1 ms to settle, enabled, before results are reliable.

registers.name: ADCSRA
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register A

fields.name: ADEN
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the ADC; writing 0 turns it off, ending any conversion in progress.

fields.name: ADSC
fields.text: Writing 1 starts a conversion in single conversion mode, or the first conversion in free running mode. The first conversion after the ADC is enabled, or started together with enabling, takes 25 ADC clocks instead of 13 and initialises the ADC. Reads 1 while a conversion runs and 0 when it completes; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ADATE
fields.text: Writing 1 enables auto triggering: a positive edge on the trigger signal chosen by ADTS in ADCSRB starts a conversion.

fields.name: ADIF
fields.text: Set at the end of a conversion, once the result is in the data registers. With ADIE and the SREG I-bit set, the conversion complete interrupt runs. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. A read-modify-write of ADCSRA, including SBI and CBI, can clear a pending interrupt.

fields.name: ADIE
fields.text: With this bit written 1 and the SREG I-bit set, the ADC conversion complete interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: ADPS
fields.text: Division factor from the system clock to the ADC input clock.

fields.name: ADC[9:8]
fields.text: ADC conversion result bits 9 and 8, right-adjusted. After ADCL is read, the data registers do not update until ADCH is read.

fields.name: ADC9
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 9.

fields.name: ADC8
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 8.

fields.name: ADC7
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 7.

fields.name: ADC6
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 6.

fields.name: ADC5
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 5.

fields.name: ADC4
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 4.

fields.name: ADC[3:2]
fields.text: ADC conversion result bits 3 and 2, left-adjusted.

fields.name: ADC
fields.text: ADC conversion result bits 7 to 0, right-adjusted. Read ADCL before ADCH; the data registers do not update again until ADCH is read.

fields.name: ADC1
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 1.

fields.name: ADC0
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 0.

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: BIN
fields.text: Gain stage mode: 0 is unipolar, the default, 1 is bipolar. Unipolar converts one-sided only, with the positive input required above the negative, saturating to the reference otherwise, at 10-bit resolution. Bipolar converts two-sided, giving a two's complement result of 9 bits plus sign.

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: Analog Comparator Multiplexer Enable.

fields.name: IPR
fields.text: Reverses the polarity of the differential input pair, so unipolar mode can measure at full 10-bit resolution with a known input polarity. An unknown polarity can first be found with a bipolar measurement, then this bit set or cleared for the following unipolar measurement.

fields.name: ADTS
fields.text: With ADATE in ADCSRA set, selects the source whose interrupt flag's rising edge triggers a conversion; with ADATE clear, it has no effect. Switching from a clear trigger source to a set one makes a positive edge, which starts a conversion if ADEN is set. Switching to free running (000) does not trigger, even with ADIF set.

fields.name: ADC0D
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the digital input buffer on the ADC0 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Set it when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused, to save power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC2D
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the digital input buffer on the ADC2 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Set it when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused, to save power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC3D
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the digital input buffer on the ADC3 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Set it when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused, to save power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC1D
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the digital input buffer on the ADC1 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Set it when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused, to save power in the buffer.

fields.name: AIN1D
fields.text: AIN1 Digital Input Disable.

fields.name: AIN0D
fields.text: AIN0 Digital Input Disable.

fields.name: DWDR7
fields.text: debugWIRE data register bit 7.

fields.name: DWDR6
fields.text: debugWIRE data register bit 6.

fields.name: DWDR5
fields.text: debugWIRE data register bit 5.

fields.name: DWDR4
fields.text: debugWIRE data register bit 4.

fields.name: DWDR3
fields.text: debugWIRE data register bit 3.

fields.name: DWDR2
fields.text: debugWIRE data register bit 2.

fields.name: DWDR1
fields.text: debugWIRE data register bit 1.

fields.name: DWDR0
fields.text: debugWIRE data register bit 0.

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register

fields.name: RSIG
fields.text: With RSIG and SPMEN set, an LPM within 3 cycles loads the device signature imprint table byte chosen by the Z-pointer into the destination register.

fields.name: CTPB
fields.text: Writing it while the temporary page buffer is being filled clears the buffer, losing its data.

fields.name: RFLB
fields.text: With RFLB and SPMEN set, an LPM within 3 cycles loads the lock bits or the fuse bits, chosen by Z0, into the destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within 4 clock cycles write a page from the temporary buffer, at the page address in the high part of Z; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the write completes or if no SPM comes within 4 cycles. The CPU halts for the whole page write.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within 4 clock cycles erase a page, at the page address in the high part of Z; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the erase completes or if no SPM comes within 4 cycles. The CPU halts during the operation.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Enables SPM for the next 4 clock cycles. Set with RSIG, CTPB, RFLB, PGWRT or PGERS, it gives the following LPM or SPM that special function; set alone, the next SPM stores R1:R0 into the temporary page buffer at the Z address, ignoring the Z LSB. Clears itself when the SPM completes or if none comes within 4 cycles; stays 1 during a page erase or write until it finishes.
